competencies.competency_text: Observes and identifies the natural (insects, plants, birds, animals, geographical features, sun and moon, stars, planets, natural resources) and social (houses, relationships) components in their immediate environment
competencies.justification: Activity 3 (write Bela's family relationship web) and Activity 4 (draw your own family with relationships) architecturally compel students to identify and name social relationships; Write tasks further require naming and classifying family members (oldest, youngest, tallest, relatives who visit)

competencies.competency_text: Describes relationships (including between humans and animals/nature) and traditions (art forms, celebrations, festivals) in the family and community
competencies.justification: 'Laughing Together' compels students to describe the human-animal relationship (pet dog Shiru as family member); 'Singing Together' and 'Helping Each Other' describe traditions — Dadiji's rain folk songs and Munni's rangoli made from dried flowers; Write tasks on relatives require describing community relationships

competencies.competency_text: Uses local materials to create simple objects (family tree, envelopes, origami animals) on their own for display or use in classroom processes
competencies.justification: Activity 2 requires students to collect fallen leaves and flowers from the ground and create a rangoli; Activity 4 requires drawing a family tree with labelled relationships — both are artefact-creation tasks using locally available or personal materials

competencies.competency_text: Describes the relationship between the natural environment and cultural practices in their immediate environment (nature of work, food, festivals, traditions)
competencies.justification: 'Singing Together' directly connects rainy season (natural environment) to family cultural practices: gathering under a garden shelter, Dadiji singing rain folk songs, and making pakodas together; 'Helping Each Other' connects dried flowers (natural material) to the rangoli tradition (cultural practice)

competencies.competency_text: Observes and describes cultural diversity in their immediate environment (food, clothing, games, different seasons, festivals related to harvest and sowing)
competencies.justification: 'Fun with Family and Friends' centres on pitthoo, a traditional street game; 'Laughing Together' features Dadaji teaching traditional games from his childhood; Find out task (p. 7) and multiple Discuss tasks require students to identify and describe games played across generations and with elders

competencies.competency_text: Learns about basic social and behavioural norms, values, and dispositions that benefit our social and natural environments and that help our society function smoothly (using dustbins, standing in queues, conserving water, using public transportation, keeping one's environment clean, always helping others in need regardless of background)
competencies.justification: 'Helping Each Other' section and Activity 1 architecturally compel students to identify household helping norms; Discuss tasks (p. 12) require reflecting on caring for grandparents, small children, and sick family members; 'Let us reflect — Discuss' extends this to caring for others beyond the family

competencies.competency_text: Presents observations and findings through different creative modes (drawing, diagram, poem, play, skit, oral and written expression)
competencies.justification: Activity 4 and Draw tasks (pp. 11, 17) require drawing; multiple Write tasks require written expression; multiple Discuss tasks require oral expression — the chapter's architecture compels students to present observations through at least three distinct creative modes
